libraries.summary: AllCore.ec is tiny (4 lines): it does `require export Core Int Real Xint` and `export Ring.IntID`. That is its ENTIRE content -- it re-exports exactly four theories (Core, Int, Real, Xint) plus the Ring.IntID sub-theory.
libraries.import_repair_note: IMPORTANT for import repair: AllCore does NOT pull in List, Distr, FSet, FMap, or any distribution/data-structure theory. Every other file in this repo that needs those explicitly writes `require import AllCore List Distr ...` etc. side-by-side. If a proof assumes `require import AllCore.` alone gives it List/Distr lemmas, that assumption is wrong under the current tree and the missing theory must be required explicitly.

libraries.summary: dbool (the uniform {0,1} distribution) is defined by CLONING Distr.MFinite at type bool with enum <- [true; false] and card <- 2, RENAMING the clone's dunifin to dbool and its dunifinE to dboolE_count. dboolE and dbool_leq are then proved directly. A `Biased` sub-theory defines dbiased p (a p-weighted coin, via clamp to keep p in [0,1]), with dbiased1E/dbiasedE/supp_dbiased/dbiased_ll/dbiased_fu, dmap_pred (relating dmap of a lossless distribution to a dbiased), and marginal_sampling_pred. `FixedBiased` is an abstract theory fixing p once via an axiom-like op declaration.
libraries.import_repair_note: The names dbool and dbool1E (etc.) are NOT primitive -- they are a renamed clone of Distr.MFinite's dunifin/dunifinE. A proof citing `dunifin`/`dunifinE` directly against DBool would need `dbool`/`dboolE_count` instead.

libraries.summary: POST-SPLIT content (see version_diffs_found): this file is now a SMALL (102-line) theory of TOTAL maps ('a,'b) map (every key has a value; from CoreMap), providing: tofun/offun (isomorphism between ('a,'b) map and 'a -> 'b functions), get/set notations, cst (constant map), map (functorial map), eq_except, and merge (pointwise combination of two maps via a 3-argument function). It requires only AllCore and CoreMap.
libraries.import_repair_note: MAJOR STRUCTURAL CHANGE, r2025.02 (#605, 'split SmtMap into SMT Array and finite map'): prior to this release, SmtMap was evidently a larger theory that also covered finite-domain map material (the kind of thing FMap.ec now provides on its own, built ON TOP OF this slimmed-down SmtMap). A proof written against a pre-r2025.02 EasyCrypt that does `require import SmtMap` expecting finite-map operations (dom, fdom, filter with a 'finite support' notion, etc.) will need to switch those specific references to FMap instead -- SmtMap.ec itself no longer has them. Anything using only total-map operations (get/set/cst/map/eq_except/merge) should be unaffected by name, though it's worth double-checking against this current (102-line) file since the surrounding theory may have been reorganized around it.
version_notes: r2025.02: MAJOR -- 'split SmtMap into SMT Array and finite map' (#605).
